versions.short: The bill would authorize the Secretary of State to set up multiyear agreements called Energy Security Pacts with eligible partner countries, aimed at strengthening energy and economic security and diversifying critical mineral and energy supply chains. It would create a Director for Energy Security Pacts and an interagency Energy Security Pacts Council to negotiate and coordinate these agreements, along with rules on eligibility, required contents such as analyses, benchmarks and financial plans, congressional notification, and a prohibition on military assistance. It would also require annual reporting and periodic evaluation by the Government Accountability Office, and would end the authority to enter new pacts 15 years after enactment.
